gloss: Of or relating to the Asian Peninsula comprising North Korea and South Korea.
Of or relating to the Korean language.
The official language of the people residing on the Korean Peninsula, and language of approximately 60 million people, in Asia, North America, and elsewhere.
A member of an East Asian ethnic group native to the Korean Peninsula.
A tree-dwelling marsupial, Phascolarctos cinereus, that resembles a small bear with a broad head, large ears and sharp claws, mainly found in eastern Australia.
A geographic region in East Asia, consisting of two countries, commonly known as South Korea and North Korea; formerly a single country.
South Korea: A country in East Asia, comprising the southern part of the Korean Peninsula.
North Korea: A country in East Asia, whose territory consists of the northern part of Korea.
A peninsula in East Asia, containing the countries of North Korea and South Korea; in full, Korean Peninsula.
Fit for use or consumption, in accordance with Jewish law (especially relating to food).
Observant of the rules of kashrut (of a person or establishment).
In accordance with standards or usual practice.
A Bantu language (or family of languages) of Central Africa.
An Ancient Greek letter representing /k/, Ϙ / ϙ, replaced by kappa by the Classical Greek period.
The Greek numeral Ϟ (lowercase ϟ), descended from the ancient letter and having the numerical value of 90.
The archaic Cyrillic numeral Ҁ (lowercase ҁ), descended from the ancient Greek letter and having the numerical value of 90.

Any of the endangered species Varanus komodoensis of monitor lizards native to certain Indonesian islands east of Java, the world's largest lizard, growing to 10 feet or 3 meters, known for its ability to kill prey with its septic saliva.
Any of several species of kingfishers in the genus Dacelo.
Any of the kanji characters invented in Japan.
A Russian monetary unit equal to one hundredth of a ruble.
A kopiyka: a Ukrainian monetary unit equal to one hundredth of a hryvnia.
A kapeyka: a Belarusian monetary unit equal to one hundredth of a ruble (rubel).
To kneel and bow low enough to touch one’s forehead to the ground.
To grovel, act in a very submissive manner; to show obeisance to (someone or something) in such a manner; to bow.
To bow very deeply.
The act of kowtowing.

The “common” Greek language that developed and flourished between 300 B.C.E. and 300 C.E. (the time of the Roman Empire), and from which Modern Greek descended. It was based on the Attic and Ionian dialects of Ancient Greek.
A surname.
A village and commune of Saaba department, Kadiogo, Centre, Burkina Faso.

A linguistic variety that has developed in supraregional contact between speakers of various interrelated dialects, typically in such a way that features shared by several dialects prevail and those of limited distribution are avoided.
A lingua franca.
Ornamental domesticated varieties of the Amur carp (Cyprinus rubrofuscus), of Japan and eastern Asia with red-gold or white coloring.

A story about a Zen master and his student, sometimes like a riddle, other times like a fable or parable, which has become an object of Zen study, and which, when meditated upon, may unlock mechanisms in the Zen student’s mind leading to satori.
A riddle with no solution, used to provoke reflection on the inadequacy of logical reasoning, and to lead to enlightenment.

A therapy technique used by Traditional Chinese medicinal physicians or medical practitioners to break a presenting patients habitual pattern of thinking that has been diagnosed as the primary cause of an illness or disease.
A fermented, effervescent, and sweetened black tea of Mongolian origin.
An Ancient Greek statue of a woman, portrayed standing, usually clothed, painted in bright colours and having an elaborate hairstyle.
Eccentric, strange, or foolish; crazy or insane; kookish.
Behaving like a kook (a person with poor style or skill); kook-like.

A partly-recognized country on the Balkan Peninsula in Southeastern Europe. Official name: Republic of Kosovo. Capital and largest city: Pristina. Considered by the Republic of Serbia to be one of its two autonomous provinces.
One of five administrative districts of the above region as viewed by the Serbian government.
An island of the Dodecanese, Greece.

A Japanese stringed instrument having numerous strings, usually seven or thirteen, that are stretched over a convex wooden sounding board and are plucked with three plectra, worn on the thumb, index finger, and middle finger of one hand.
Edible kelp (“a type of brown seaweed”) (from the class Phaeophyceae) used in East Asian cuisine.
A type of harp or lute played in West Africa.
A non-contact unisex team sport originating from the Netherlands, similar to netball, where players attempt to throw a ball into a basket atop a pole.
The ball used in the sport of korfball.
A member of the indigenous peoples of the Konkan coast of India.
An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Konkan region of India.
Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes, a variety of the cabbage, having a turnip-shaped edible stem.
The rise in popularity of South Korean popular culture in other countries since the 1990s.
A dark powder, usually powdered stibnite (an antimony ore), used as eye makeup, especially in Eastern countries.
A war fought in the Korean Peninsula from 1950–1953 between the Soviet Union-backed Democratic People's Republic of Korea and the United Nations-backed Republic of Korea.
A situation of formal war that is de jure in progress since the 1950s on the Korean Peninsula, that has not had a formal resolution and peace treaty, but only has a longstanding armistice in place.
Any of various spicy meatball or meatloaf dishes of the Middle East, Caucasus, South Asia, and the Balkans.
A peninsula in East Asia, containing the countries of North Korea and South Korea.
A fermented drink made from mare's milk, common among peoples of the Central Asian steppes.
An independent city in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, at the confluence of the Rhine and Moselle Rivers.

A foul-smelling plant grown in Asia, Amorphophallus konjac.
Any of various food products made from the plant, including a flour and a gelatin, used to make noodles and candies, and as a food supplement for weight reduction.
A Ukrainian and Russian couple-dance with constantly increasing tempo.
A peninsula in Murmansk Oblast, in the far north of Russia. It borders upon the Barents Sea on the north and the White Sea on the east and south.

The capital city of Kōchi Prefecture, Japan.
A prefecture of Japan.

The process whereby a lect develops into a koine, or an instance of this.
A traditional Russian headdress worn by women and girls to accompany the sarafan.

One of the Songhay languages of Mali.
